issues.rootCause: Missing port passed API/provision URL validation and let pg select PGPORT/default; migrate accepted port zero. Another matching local database instance could be selected unintentionally. No observed database incident.
issues.change: All three entries require an explicit nonzero URL port. Preserve loopback, role, database, query/fragment constraints. Update protected-environment contract; other PG credential/TLS/options remain environment-dependent.

issues.rootCause: Open queued behind a blocked delete may wait indefinitely and receives no blocked event itself. Normal open of existing v1 is not an upgrade blocked by other v1 connections.
issues.change: Reject on own blocked or a 10-second wait deadline; clear timer on blocked/error/success; abort late upgrade and close late successful connection. Deadline does not cancel underlying request or unblock deletion; background suspension can delay timer execution.

verification.specification: W3C IndexedDB connection queues and opening/deletion algorithms; static reasoning, not runtime reproduction

issues.limitation: Storage prerequisite only. Lock covers commit, not provider load/generation. Caller-provided sealedState is not a validated MLS provider snapshot.

issues.rootCause: A committed registration with lost response left session.deviceId stale and no session refresh entry. Errors could be described as registration failure.
issues.change: Refresh directory after success or failure, report unconfirmed outcome, and provide explicit session-and-device refresh via parent query/remount. Apply directory refresh to revocation too.
issues.limitation: Manual refresh unmounts the old workspace and releases its local message; no credential or MLS trust is created.

issues.rootCause: A committed invitation revocation with lost response left the old list unchanged and no direct refresh.
issues.change: Refresh authoritative queries in finally; add manual registration/invitation refresh; retain outcome message outside query contents. Existing server revocation remains idempotent.
